Years 11–13 Social
Sciences – Commerce

Learning expectations
Through the Commerce subjects, students develop strong foundations in economic, financial, and
business thinking, decision-making, and problem-solving. They are taught to understand and
analyse how individuals, businesses, and communities make economic and financial decisions,
and how these decisions influence and are influenced by the wider world.

The learning area supports students to think critically, make informed decisions, evaluate
economic and financial information, and apply commerce knowledge and skills in personal,
business, and wider economic contexts.

Key features of the refreshed learning area
•   Clear progression from Years 9–10 Economic Activity through to specialist pathways in
    Accounting, Business Studies and Economics.
•   Strong emphasis on critical thinking, problem-solving, and informed economic, financial, and
    business decision-making.
•   Accounting includes an explicit strand on Accounting for Entrepreneurship.
•   Explicit teaching of disciplinary writing and communication, to help students analyse evidence
    and justify decisions and recommendations.
•   Restructuring of the Year 11 Commerce subject, with Accounting established as a standalone
    subject across Years 11–13 and Business and Economics combined in a foundational Year 11
    subject before separating into individual subjects in Years 12–13.
•   Business Studies provides flexibility to use student-led businesses, case studies, and a range
    of contexts, including agribusiness.
•   Economics is now divided into strands based around Microeconomic and Macroeconomic
    content across both year levels.
•   Strong connections between theory and real-world contexts, including business, economics,
    finance, entrepreneurship, organisations, markets, and decision-making.


Subjects
Subjects within the Social Sciences – Commerce learning area are:

•   Years 11–13 Accounting
•   Year 11 Business and Economics
•   Years 12–13 Business Studies
•   Years 12–13 Economics.

Learning and pathways

Years 11–13 Accounting

Students are taught how financial and non-financial information supports decision-making in
businesses and organisations. They apply accounting concepts and practices to interpret and
communicate information, assess financial performance and position, and inform planning and
improvement.

Strands

Years 11–13 Accounting is organised into four subject strands and a disciplinary writing strand:

•   Accounting Systems and Processes
•   Financial Reporting
•   Accounting Analysis and Decision Making
•   Accounting for Entrepreneurship
•   Disciplinary Writing.

Pathways

Years 11–13 Accounting leads to pathways in accounting and related fields, such as commerce,
finance, and economics.


Year 11 Business and Economics

Students are taught how businesses, consumers, and governments interact in the economy, and
how financial and economic reasoning informs decision-making. They apply theory and models to
a range of business contexts, including marketing, people management, planning, and operations,
and consider how internal and external factors affect businesses.

Strands

Year 11 Business and Economics is organised into four subject strands and a disciplinary writing
strand:

•   Scarcity and the Market
•   Allocation of Resources and the Circular Flow
•   Business and the Business Environment
•   Enterprise, Entrepreneurship, and Innovation
•   Disciplinary Writing.

Pathways

Year 11 Business and Economics provides foundations for further study in Business Studies and
Economics as well as other social sciences learning areas and related pathways in Years 12 and
13. It contributes to pathways in fields such as commerce, law, public service, and agribusiness.

Years 12–13 Business Studies

Students are taught core business concepts, frameworks, and practices that explain how
businesses create value, develop enterprise, operate, grow, and respond to change. Through their
own businesses or case studies, they examine how businesses manage resources, respond to
stakeholders, and develop competitive advantage. They explore decision-making across strategy,
finance, marketing, people, operations, risk, and sustainability.

Strands

Years 12–13 Business Studies is organised into four subject strands and a disciplinary writing
strand:

•   Enterprise and Growth
•   Strategic Business Management and Sustainability
•   Creating Value
•   Workforce and Financial Viability
•   Disciplinary Writing.

Pathways

Year 12–13 Business Studies leads to pathways in business, economics, commerce, agribusiness,
and related fields such as entrepreneurship, management, commercial innovation, agri-innovation,
rural enterprise, and environmental leadership.


Years 12–13 Economics

Students are taught how economic decisions and events affect societies, and how scarcity and
choice influence economic outcomes. They apply economic concepts, models, and values to
understand how consumers, businesses, governments, and communities interact and make
decisions.

Strands

Years 12–13 Economics is organised into two subject strands and a disciplinary writing strand:

•   Microeconomics
•   Macroeconomics
•   Disciplinary Writing.

Pathways

Years 12–13 Economics leads to pathways in related areas such as business, finance, public
policy, and global development.

Connections to other learning areas
Commerce connects strongly with:

•   Mathematics and Statistics through financial calculations, quantitative analysis, modelling,
    forecasting, and interpretation of data.
•   Social Sciences through economic systems, government policy, societal change, consumer
    behaviour, and the relationships between individuals, businesses, and communities.
•   Technology through innovation, digital business, information systems, artificial intelligence, and
    changing ways of producing and exchanging goods and services.
•   Science through sustainability, resource use, innovation, and the use of scientific evidence in
    business and economic decision-making.
•   English through disciplinary writing, interpretation, and communication of financial and
    economic information, evaluation of evidence and communication for different audiences and
    purposes.


How to design a programme
•   The knowledge and practice statements within each element are related, but teachers may
    select complementary statements from across the sequence or treat elements as discrete units
    of work. Disciplinary writing is most effectively taught when integrated across the teaching
    programme.
•   In Accounting, within the Accounting for Entrepreneurship strand, students will engage in an
    investigation about long-term business sustainability in different contexts.
•   Within Year 11 Business & Economics, the practices in the Business and the Business
    Environment and the Enterprise, Entrepreneurship, and Innovation strands may be taught
    through either teacher provided case studies or student-generated ideas. Student-generated
    ideas may be developed for real-world sale or explored as innovative concepts that are not
    taken to market.
•   For Years 12–13 Business Studies, the programme uses authentic local, national, and global
    contexts, disciplinary models and frameworks, and a range of evidence sources, including
    data, reports, financial information, case studies, and contemporary issues. A context table is
    included in the curriculum document to show the range of contexts, along with a supporting
    document specific to agribusiness.
